newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche H1 operating margin drops.
newsitem.headline: Roche H1 operating margin drops.

text.p: Roche Holding AG said on Friday its operating profit margin in the first half of 1997 fell to 22.1 percent from 25 percent last year due to price pressures, expiry of patents, heavy pre-marketing costs and accelerated research and development.
But despite a lower operating margin, higher cost of goods sales and operating costs, Roche's operating profit rose five percent to 2.06 billion francs, the company said in its half-year report.
While Roche's sales rose 19.7 percent to 9.3 billion Swiss francs in the first half, the cost of sales rose 27.4 percent to 3.03 billion and operating costs rose 22.6 percent to 4.2 billion.

Roche's gross profit margin fell to 67.4 percent from 69 percent due to the adverse affect of heavy price pressures and a "certain unfavourable sales mix developments due to patent expiries," the company said.
Roche's patent on the anti-epileptic drug Rivotril/Klonopin has expired and the company said it was facing "massive generic competition" to the drug.

"Marketing and distribution expenses were substantially higher compared to the corresponding preceding-year period," Roche said, attributing the rise to exchange rate developments, expanded activities in new markets and "in particular, costs related to premarketing and sales force build-up for new product introductions."
Roche has expanded its global sales force markedly ahead of the broad-based roll-out of new drugs and in the U.S. alone more than 1,000 new positions have been created since 1996.
Roche also said there were costs from integrating flavourings company Tastemaker -- the acquisition was approved end-March.
Roche's research and development costs also rose 26 percent to 1.4 billion francs due to higher exchange rates of most foreign currencies and accelerated product development.

Roche's non-operating income rose 17.8 percent to 926 million francs, primarily due to gains on the sale of marketable securities and net currency exchange gains due to favourable developments on capital and foreign currency markets.
